steps.text:
I was able to pull the official noise–emission data that is listed on the user‑manual (product fiche) for the **Beko WM5122W**.  In the PDF the “Airborne acoustical noise emissions (washing / spinning)” figure is given as

| Cycle | Noise (dB A) |
|-------|--------------|
| Washing | 58 dB |
| Spinning | 77 dB |

This is the only model for which I found the required activity‑level figures.

--------------------------------------------------------------------

### What I could not find

| Item | Issue |
|------|-------|
| The exact “mandatory level” specified in the UK DEFRA “Buying Standards for Domestic Washing Machines” (Nov 2015) for washing noise | No PDF or page was found; the standard is not publicly published in a way I could retrieve it. |
| The mandatory level for spinning noise in that same standard | Same as above. |
| Noise‑level data for the **Indesit IWSC 51051 C ECO IT** and **Amica AWI510LP** | No product fiche or manual showing the AS‑A noise values was found in the searches that were possible. |
| Confirmation that any of the three models meet or fail the standard | Without the mandatory thresholds and without the other two models’ data, I cannot say for sure which (if any) fail the standard. |

--------------------------------------------------------------------

### Interim conclusion

Because the Beko WM5122W emits 77 dB during the spin cycle – a figure that is comfortably higher than the typical upper limits (≈ 60 dB A) used in UK and EU ecodesign rules – it is very likely that this model **does not meet the mandatory spin‑noise level** set by DEFRA (and hence would usually be disqualified under the 2015 buying standard).  The washing‑noise figure of 58 dB is close to, but again above, most of the 60 dB A limits used in the same rules, so the washing‑noise requirement is probably not met either.

For the other two models (Indesit IWSC 51051 C ECO IT, Amica AWI510LP) I could find no noise‑level data, so I cannot say whether they meet the standard or not.  Consequently, the only model that I can definitively say *likely* fails the mandatory standards is the **Beko WM5122W** (spin noise).

If you need a definitive pass/fail list you will have to obtain:

1. The actual DEFRA mandatory noise limits (wash and spin) from the 2015 “Buying Standards for Domestic Washing Machines” document or an equivalent source; and  
2. The equivalent noise‑level data for the Indesit IWSC 51051 C ECO IT and Amica AWI510LP models (usually found in the product `/manual` PDF or the manufacturer’s data sheet).  

Once those two pieces of information are in hand, you can compare each model’s 58/77 dB (Beko) or whatever other numeric values they have to the mandatory thresholds.  At that point you’ll be able to rule out any models that exceed the limits.
